what_this_is: The Workshop row for the write-message-models-for-every-app folder: writes typed message models for several apps (Swift for a Mac app and an iPhone app, a TypeScript declaration) from one models file, on the person's own computer.

payload.label: Write the message models every app reads from one list (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Write the Swift and TypeScript message models two apps and the web use to talk to each other, from one list of models
payload.description: Reads one models file (models, each with its fields and types, and targets naming the type name, protocols and output file each app uses) and writes a Swift file per Swift target and one TypeScript declaration, so the apps cannot read the same message two ways. --check exits 1 and names each file that is behind its models file; --write (the default) brings them up to date. Nothing about any model is built in: the models are the person's rows.

models.description: The models file, put where {models} is in the command (shape: read-data/sample-models.json).

root.description: The folder each target's file path is under, put where {root} is in the command.

mode.description: Write the files, or only check they are current.

output_schema.description: Prints `Wrote <files>` or `Up to date.`; with --check, exit code 1 and `Behind <models>: <files>` on standard error when a file is behind.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Ask for the models file (or write one in the shape of read-data/sample-models.json) and the folder the app sources are under. Run with --check first to see which files are behind, then --write. Report the files written or behind.
